commentary: Under O'Neil's market-direction discipline and Stan Weinstein's stage analysis, a healthy market requires broad participation and an absence of institutional distribution. With market breadth deteriorated at 40 and 41 Nifty laggards against just 9 gainers amid rising volatility, the tape sits under distribution pressure. Jesse Livermore consistently warned against fighting the general trend, as three out of four equities inevitably follow index direction. Minervini's progressive exposure framework strictly dictates capital preservation, holding cash, and cutting exposure when the deterministic gate signals weakness. In the absence of constructive Stage 2 breakouts from sound volatility contraction patterns, sitting out and protecting capital is the only sound tactical posture.
